summary: The candidate correctly binds all four raw reviewer responses to the substantive sealed lane payload and enforces the intended Git lane order, but its declared identity key has two fail-open cases. A reused agent/human stable reviewerId is treated as independent when only provider changes, and a model-assisted record may omit the resolved model then obtain a new identity by changing only the requested alias. These are concrete declared-metadata bypasses, not demands for cryptographic personhood, so candidate ee42f352 must not become the v2 baseline until fixed and covered by full-chain mutations.

findings.title: Provider changes defeat stable agent/human reviewerId reuse detection
findings.contract: The methodology says agent/human lanes use an explicit stable reviewerId, and the candidate-1 disposition says the validator rejects reused declared identities.

evidence.detail: Lane D requires the verifier to differ from completeness, blind, and comparison roles and says agent/human identity is the stable reviewerId.
S6-001 is bounded on the express premise that reused declared identities are rejected and runtime handoffs cover attribution.
reviewer_identity() returns (kind, reviewerId, provider) for agent and human reviewers, so provider is incorrectly part of the stable-actor key.
Every completeness/blind/comparator/verifier separation check relies on that tuple inequality.

reproduction.whyInThreatModel: The declarations retain the same stable reviewerId and kind; no relabeling of the actor is needed. Only an otherwise non-authoritative provider/channel field changes, so this bypasses the promised declared-identity check before any runtime-attribution trust boundary is reached.

findings.impact: One agent or human can occupy completeness plus blind, comparator, or verifier roles while preserving the same declared stable reviewerId. The lane artifact can pass the exact inequality checks that are supposed to enforce independence.
minimalFix: For non-model reviewers, key identity only by the documented stable actor key, at minimum (kind, reviewerId); do not include provider, requested/response model, run ID, prompt path, or response path.
Keep dishonest kind/reviewerId relabeling as the explicitly documented runtime-handoff trust boundary rather than pretending the validator proves personhood.
Add full-chain mutations showing that the same agent and the same human remain non-independent when provider, model fields, request mode, or prompt/response paths change.

findings.title: Empty resolved model falls back to a caller-controlled requested alias
findings.contract: The methodology defines model-assisted identity as provider plus resolved model; changing a run ID or response path must not create independence.

evidence.detail: The model identity contract is provider plus resolved model and requires exact requested/response tags.
For model-assisted records reviewer_identity() uses responseModel or requestedModel, making requestedModel an identity fallback when responseModel is empty.
validate_reviewer() checks envelope equality but never requires provider or responseModel to be nonempty.

The shared reviewer shape requires provider and responseModel only to be strings; empty strings validate. The same shape is repeated in blind-derivation.schema.json lines 161-223, comparison.schema.json lines 147-209, and audit-result.schema.json lines 170-232.

observed: All four reviewer schemas accepted provider='ollama-cloud', responseModel='', and requestedModel='alias-a'.
validate_reviewer() returned the substantive payload with zero failures for both alias-a and alias-b successful envelopes.
reproduction.whyInThreatModel: This uses schema-valid, provenance-matching successful response envelopes. No actor relabeling is required; the candidate itself substitutes the requested alias for missing runtime resolution.

findings.impact: If the runtime/provider does not supply a nonempty resolved model tag, repeated use of the same unresolved model can be presented as independent merely by requesting two aliases. The artifact no longer proves the provider-plus-resolved-model identity promised by the methodology.
minimalFix: Conditionally require nonempty provider and responseModel for kind=model-assisted in every reviewer schema and in validate_reviewer().
Build model identity from provider plus responseModel only; fail closed instead of falling back to requestedModel.
Add full-chain negative controls for empty provider, empty responseModel, and two requested aliases with the same missing/identical resolved model.

verifiedControls.evidence: validate_reviewer() parses hash-pinned raw responses; completeness at scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:1077-1094, blind at 1143-1155, comparator at 1402-1418, and verifier at 1563-1579 require exact equality with their sealed substantive lane payloads. The 73-test suite includes the unrelated-comparator-response rejection and passed.
Completeness and blind prompts are rebuilt and byte-compared at scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:679-698,1095-1109,1118-1141; the blind prompt also receives forbidden-token checks.

Schemas are closed; comparison cannot embed verification/final resolution, adjudication references rather than restates comparison, and validator role checks are present. The only reproduced separation bypasses are S6-R06-001 and S6-R06-002.

Declared UTC times must strictly increase packet < completeness < blind at scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:1204-1210, blind < comparison at 1461-1464, and comparison < adjudication at 1644-1647. Git-derived pre-seal/direct-child ordering is additionally enforced at 1043-1049,1113-1116,1265-1272,1487-1495, and all 140 comparisons must exist before adjudication at 1896-1929. Git ancestry, not self-declared wall time, is the authoritative lane-order evidence.

verifiedControls.control: Same provider plus nonempty resolved model ignores run/path changes
verifiedControls.evidence: reviewer_identity() ignores reviewerId and response path for model-assisted reviewers, and test_same_model_with_different_response_paths_is_not_independent passed.

s6TrustBoundary.conclusion: S6-001 has an inherent runtime-attribution part that is explicitly bounded, but the current disposition overstates the mechanical layer. The harness cannot prove that a human name, Hermes subagent ID, model tag, or prompt-delivery attestation is truthful; that is not a reasonable cryptographic-personhood requirement. Final execution must retain and independently reconcile actual Hermes subagent/delegation IDs, role assignments, separate workspace lock paths, exact delivered prompt bytes/hashes, exact returned response bytes/hashes, and handoff order. Comparator/verifier prompt adequacy and the truth of agent/human kind/reviewerId remain runtime checks because those prompts are only hash-pinned, not canonically rebuilt from all inspected inputs. Declared sealedAtUtc values are attestations; Git commit ancestry is the mechanical order proof. However S6-R06-001 and S6-R06-002 are concrete bypasses inside the declared metadata contract and must be fixed before relying on that bounded runtime handoff.
mechanicallyEnforced: exact prompt/response file hashes and seal-commit bytes
canonical completeness and blind prompt bytes
raw-response equality to the substantive sealed lane payload
strict declared timestamp order plus Git lane ancestry
runtimeEvidenceStillRequired: actual Hermes subagent or human identity corresponding to stable reviewerId
no relabeling of kind or reviewerId across roles
actual provider and resolved model returned by the runtime
actual prompt bytes delivered to comparator/verifier and sufficient inspected inputs
separate workspace roots and held root locks for independent workers
dispatch/return ordering consistent with the sealed lane commits
s6TrustBoundary.prelockState: No substantive Stage 1 lane has run: prelock validation reports all 140 units pending-blind-derivation. Therefore no future runtime handoff can be certified by this rereview; the final integrator must inspect it before acceptance.

residualRisks: Even after the two mechanical fixes, declared human/agent provenance cannot establish cryptographic personhood. The final runtime-handoff reconciliation in s6TrustBoundary is mandatory.

Comparator and verifier prompts are committed and hash-pinned but not canonically generated from every revealed/verified input; independent runtime inspection must confirm that those workers actually received sufficient inputs.
sealedAtUtc records ordering attestations rather than trustworthy wall-clock acquisition times; Git ancestry is the durable order boundary.
